title: Common IT Words
summary: Beginner-friendly glossary for common IT department terms.
purpose: Mentors and tickets use these words every shift. Knowing them lets you follow conversations and ask sharper questions.

title: What Does IT Do?
summary: Plain-language overview of what an IT department supports.
purpose: Seeing the big picture helps you understand why each task matters and who depends on it.

title: Domain Basics
summary: What a managed domain means for accounts, computers, and access.
purpose: Most campus computers and accounts are managed centrally. This explains why some changes need IT staff approval.

title: Configuration Manager Overview
summary: Beginner-safe overview of SCCM / Configuration Manager.
purpose: You will hear about software being pushed to computers. This helps you recognize it without changing anything yourself.

title: Computer Imaging Overview
summary: Mental model for imaging without exposing internal procedures.
purpose: Imaging prepares computers for use. Knowing the idea helps you assist safely and stop when something looks wrong.

title: Ticket Basics
summary: How tickets help IT track requests, issues, and draft notes.
purpose: Tickets are how IT keeps track of work. Clear notes help the next person pick up where you left off.

title: Asset Tag Basics
summary: How asset tags identify equipment and prevent mix-ups.
purpose: Asset tags prevent mix-ups between devices. Checking them is one of the first beginner-safe tasks you may do.

title: Hardware Basics
summary: Common hardware terms, safe checks, and escalation boundaries.
purpose: Many requests start with a cable, monitor, or power issue. This covers safe first checks and when to stop.

title: How to Ask for Help
summary: How to prepare clear mentor questions and summaries.
purpose: Asking early with clear details saves time for you and your mentor. This shows you how.

title: Escalation Rules
summary: When to stop, document, and ask a mentor or supervisor.
purpose: Knowing when to stop and ask keeps you, users, and equipment safe. This is one of the most important habits in IT.
